baseline.versionPolicy: Stable trust-boundary and ownership outcomes apply across Tauri 2 releases; verify capability, permission, plugin, platform WebView, and build mechanisms against pinned dependencies.

owns: filesystem, network, database, and sidecar adaptation

hardOutcomes: Effective capabilities and permissions do not exceed actual feature needs.
Static dependencies are acyclic and state mutations do not bypass their owner.
The WebView remains an untrusted caller of Rust authority.

invariants.outcome: Every IPC operation treats the WebView as untrusted, validates and authorizes the concrete Rust-side resource action, and exposes only least-privilege capabilities and permissions.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Custom commands, plugins, or other protocols comply when effective permission inspection and hostile-input tests prove equivalent resource scoping and authorization.

invariants.outcome: Frontend modules, Rust modules, crates, and workspace packages are acyclic, and every business fact, shared resource, and cross-module write has an explicit owner.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Any feature and crate layout qualifies when dependency evidence and mutation paths prove the same ownership and do not bypass public boundaries.

invariants.outcome: Every adopted managed state value, listener, channel, long task, lock, database write, window, and sidecar has bounded ownership, conflict, termination, and cleanup semantics.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Different synchronization and lifecycle mechanisms qualify when concurrency and shutdown tests prove no orphan work, unsafe cross-await locks, stale writes, or resource leaks.

invariants.outcome: Secrets, credentials, signing keys, logs, and every adopted remote WebView, update, CSP, and transport mechanism preserve the declared code and secret trust boundaries.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: CSP or a verified equivalent control complies for remote content when hostile-origin tests prove it cannot gain unintended IPC or data authority; signing material must remain outside delivered clients and logs.

invariants.outcome: All Commands are registered at exactly one invoke_handler point with unique names, and actual IPC names, request and response fields, and structured errors remain synchronized between every producer and consumer.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: A generated registry, a single explicit generate_handler invocation, or another composition mechanism qualifies when static or integration evidence proves one effective registration point, unique names, and matching producer-consumer contracts.

invariants.outcome: Supported development and production bundles are reproducible from a clean checkout using declared Rust, adopted JavaScript, platform, configuration, permission, generated, and packaging inputs.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Any workspace and frontend toolchain comply when repository commands bind the actual capabilities and delivered bundle without absolute paths or undeclared machine changes.

proves: The repository-selected production Tauri bundle path completes on the active platform.
doesNotProve: Other platforms, signing custody, updater behavior, or runtime authorization is correct.

proves: The repository-selected frontend tests pass for exercised feature and IPC consumer behavior.
doesNotProve: Rust-side authorization or native resource cleanup is correct.

proves: Rust workspace tests pass for the active platform and exercised adapters.
doesNotProve: The final WebView permission union or unexercised platform integrations are secure.

scenarios.failure: A compromised or remote WebView invokes a broad command or supplies a hostile path, URL, sidecar argument, tenant, or resource identifier that escapes its authority.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Enumerate the effective capability union and exercise malformed, traversal, hostile-origin, cross-owner, and overbroad resource requests against Rust-side checks.

scenarios.failure: A Command is registered twice or at a second invoke_handler point, or a producer changes an IPC name, field, or structured error without updating an actual consumer.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Inspect the effective command registry and exercise or mechanically compare every adopted producer-consumer contract; prove one registration point, unique names, and synchronized request, response, and error shapes.

scenarios.failure: A window closes or the application exits while a listener, channel, lock, database write, or sidecar remains orphaned or writes through disposed state.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Exercise window and process termination during active work, cancel and join owners with bounds, and verify dependent resources close in order.
